**Scope.** This report covers only the `mongodb.com/atlas-reconciliation-policy: "skip"` annotation of the Atlas Kubernetes Operator (AKO). It covers how the operator parses the annotation, what a skipped reconcile does and does not do, how it interacts with deletion and finalizers, what happens when the annotation is removed, and where MongoDB's documentation and code disagree. Out of scope: the sibling annotations (`atlas-resource-policy`, `atlas-resource-version-policy`) except where they interact with skip, dry-run mode, the subobject→independent-CRD migration as a topic, and Terraform/AKO

1. [CODE] The operator reads only `metadata.annotations["mongodb.com/atlas-reconciliation-policy"]`, and skips only when the value equals the exact string `skip`. Any other value, including `Skip`, `SKIP`, `true` or `keep`, does not skip. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongodb-atlas-kubernetes/main/internal/controller/customresource/customresource.go 2. [CODE] A *label* with this key has no effect, because `ReconciliationShouldBeSkipped` calls `GetAnnotations()` and never `GetLabels()`.

When an AtlasProject, AtlasDeployment or AtlasIPAccessList is skipped and has a deletionTimestamp, the controller removes the AKO finalizer and returns without running Atlas-side deletion. AtlasDatabaseUser differs: its skip() only logs and returns workflow.OK(), and no code between PrepareResource and the skip check handles deletionTimestamp or finalizers.
